findings.current: The swift, concise first form of the Flame Divine Palm.
findings.defect: The Korean says 일 초, meaning a single move or technique, not necessarily the first form. “First form” adds an ordinal and changes the technique description.
findings.rationale: The source describes one swift, concise move of the Flame Divine Palm; it does not establish that this is the technique's first form.
findings.replacement: A swift, concise move of the Flame Divine Palm.

findings.current: The kind of bastard who looked capable of crawling back alive even if he were thrown into the deepest pit of the underworld.
findings.defect: “Crawling back” adds a manner of movement and an image of weakened return that the source does not establish.
findings.rationale: The Korean says he would seem capable of returning alive from the bottom of the underworld; it emphasizes survival, not crawling or physical exhaustion.
findings.replacement: The kind of bastard who looked capable of coming back alive even if he were thrown into the deepest pit of the underworld.

findings.current: A figure shot from the water atop a towering spray and landed heavily on the sandy shore.
findings.defect: “Atop a towering spray” places the figure on top of the water column, whereas the source says he surged upward together with the tall stream of water.
findings.rationale: 함께 means “together with” here; the source presents the spray accompanying his emergence, not him standing or riding atop it.
findings.replacement: A figure shot up with a towering spray and landed heavily on the sandy shore.

summary: The chapter is largely faithful, with three minor source-fidelity regressions involving technique count, an added physical image, and the positioning of the returning figure.
